sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, and covers the north-western edge of Bordentown above the Delaware River. Farnsworth Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet from Courtland (printed Cortland) Street to West Park Street, with Prince Street parallel to it along the lower third. 2nd Street closes the top edge, where the sheet joins sheet 3. The upper half holds Farnsworth Avenue's commercial row on the north side: stores, a canned goods store, a garage with wagon shed, the Fire Department's Hose Co. No. 2 house, rows of brick-filled dwellings and an apartment building at the corner of East Park Street. McKnights Avenue and McKnights Alley run north from Farnsworth Avenue past small dwellings, and City Park lies at the left behind the top of a steep bank. An inclined drive with stone retaining walls drops from Farnsworth Avenue toward the river. South of Farnsworth Avenue the blocks hold large dwellings with summer houses on big lots, and below Prince Street are more dwellings and the Yapewi Aquatic Club on the water. At the left, below a steep bank, the Pennsylvania Railroad (Trenton Division) runs down the sheet beside the Delaware River, the City Dock and the Riverview Iron Works, with a machine shop and a battery charging station. The compass and scale bar are at the lower left and a Bordentown oval stamp at the right.
notes: Cortland is printed for what OpenStreetMap calls Courtland Street.
McKnights Avenue is McKnight Avenue in OpenStreetMap; it was not used for control.
The detected junction of 2nd Street with Park Street at the right edge and 2nd Street with Courtland Street at the top rest on the top edge of the sheet and were kept.
Farnsworth Avenue, Prince, Cortland and Park Streets on the bluff above the Delaware River; City Park, Riverview Iron Works, City Dock; north up-left; 50 ft. Configured by a helper.

sheet-3-1.description: Part 1 is the main part of sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, in the north-west corner of Bordentown above the Crosswicks Creek. North points to the upper right. It covers the blocks between 2nd Street and 3rd Street from Bank Street south through Thompson Street to East Park Street, with the bluff above Crosswicks Creek along the top. On the creek bank, below a steep slope, stand the buildings of the Rice Gas Engine Co., marked not in operation and partly vacated, with a machine shop, office, test house and watchman's house, together with boat sheds and the boat house of the Rice Athletic Club. The Pennsylvania Railroad crosses the creek at the upper left on a wooden trestle beside a foot bridge. Bank Street and Thompson Street are lined with rows of small brick-filled dwellings. The large block south of Thompson Street holds the canning factory of the Estate of A. Brakeley, with its factory buildings, store house, box nailing and storage building, pea and bean shelling machines, pump house and a 10,000 gallon tank on a steel tower, and a cement block factory. Along 3rd Street and East Park Street are dormitories of the B.M.I. students (Bordentown Military Institute). East of 3rd Street the vacant private grounds of Harris H. Hammond are marked. The left edge is the heavy line separating part 2 of the sheet.
notes: Drawn with north up-right, turned 90 degrees from the downtown sheets.
McKnight Street is printed M'Knight St.; it is not in OpenStreetMap as a street.

Two parts, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Bank Street to East Park Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets, Rice Gas Engine Co. and Crosswicks Creek at the top; drawn with north up-right (rotation about +31). Part 2: West Burlington Street from Pine Street (not opened) south to Black's Creek, behind a heavy line at the lower left, drawn at the main town's orientation; anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-3-2.description: Part 2 is the strip at the left of sheet 3, set off by a heavy line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, at the orientation of the downtown sheets rather than of the main part. It shows West Burlington Street running south from Pine Street, which is marked not opened, to Black's Creek at the bottom of the sheet. The land on the west side of the street is mostly open, with a few one- and two-storey dwellings and the work car and tool house of the Public Service Railway Co. Lot numbers 201 to 213 and 216 to 229 are printed along the two sides of the street, and a 4 inch water pipe runs down it. Black's Creek crosses at the bottom, where the street continues onto sheet 13.
notes: Pine Street is marked not opened; West Pine Street in OpenStreetMap meets West Burlington Street at this point.
Anchored on one hand-picked junction (West Burlington / Pine) with the scale of the atlas and a north direction of -66 degrees from the bearing of West Burlington Street; low confidence.

Two parts, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Bank Street to East Park Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets, Rice Gas Engine Co. and Crosswicks Creek at the top; drawn with north up-right (rotation about +31). Part 2: West Burlington Street from Pine Street (not opened) south to Black's Creek, behind a heavy line at the lower left, drawn at the main town's orientation; anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-4-1.description: Part 1 is the main part of sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. It covers the western edge of Bordentown along Prince Street, from West Park Street at the top through West Church Street to Walnut Street and Willow Street, and the low ground west of it down to the Delaware River and Black's Creek. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs across the upper half of the part: its station, freight depot and shops lie between the driveway to the depot and Railroad Avenue, where Prince Street passes over the tracks on a wooden bridge. Below the railroad, beside a stone retaining wall, are a coal yard and an ice plant. Christ Episcopal Church, its rectory and a graveyard stand on Prince Street at West Church Street, with an old graveyard behind them, and Prince Street and Walnut Street are lined with two- and three-storey dwellings. The steep bank along the railroad, a driveway down to the river and the mouth of Black's Creek fill the western half. Two insets with heavy borders are cut out of the part: the Ash Springs pumping station at the upper left and Fieldsboro at the lower left.
notes: Prince Street / West Park Street and Prince Street / West Church Street were hand-picked: the detector placed both 37 to 43 ft off on lot lines.
Railroad Avenue ends in a foot path at Prince Street, which crosses the railroad on a wooden bridge.

Three parts, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Prince Street between West Park and Walnut Streets, Pennsylvania Railroad station and shops, Christ Episcopal Church, Delaware River and Black's Creek; north up-right. Part 2 (inset, top left): Pumping Station of City of Bordentown at Ash Springs, Mercer County, 3 miles NE of City Hall: no street, not placed. Part 3 (inset, lower left): Fieldsboro, Front Street to 2nd Street along Hamilton Street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Pumping Station of City of Bordentown, Ash Springs, Mercer County, 3 miles NE of City Hall (no street junction; outside the reference box; needs a modern feature at the pumping station).

sheet-4-3.description: Part 3 is an inset in the lower left corner of sheet 4, inside a heavy border, showing the north end of Fieldsboro at 50 feet to an inch. It covers Front Street and 2nd Street on either side of Hamilton Street, in the blocks numbered 10, 11 and 135 to 137, with the top of a steep slope down to the railroad along its upper edge, about 125 feet from the tracks. Most buildings are one- and two-storey frame and brick-filled dwellings with sheds; a public school stands on 2nd Street at Hamilton Street. A borough line runs along the right edge of the inset. The rest of Fieldsboro continues on sheet 15.
notes: Front is North Front Street and 2nd Street is North 2nd Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from two points: Front / Hamilton detected and 2nd / Hamilton hand-picked (helmert); low confidence.

Three parts, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Prince Street between West Park and Walnut Streets, Pennsylvania Railroad station and shops, Christ Episcopal Church, Delaware River and Black's Creek; north up-right. Part 2 (inset, top left): Pumping Station of City of Bordentown at Ash Springs, Mercer County, 3 miles NE of City Hall: no street, not placed. Part 3 (inset, lower left): Fieldsboro, Front Street to 2nd Street along Hamilton Street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Pumping Station of City of Bordentown, Ash Springs, Mercer County, 3 miles NE of City Hall (no street junction; outside the reference box; needs a modern feature at the pumping station).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, and covers downtown Bordentown. Farnsworth Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, crossed by West Park and East Park at the top, Railroad Avenue, West Church and East Church in the middle and Walnut below. Prince Street runs down the left side and 2nd Street down the right. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Trenton Division) crosses between stone retaining walls in a tunnel under Farnsworth Avenue, with a wooden bridge at each end. The commercial blocks along Farnsworth Avenue hold the Bordentown Register printing office, the Bordentonian Theatre, the Post Office, Earlings Hotel, Central Hotel, the Community House and Library, drugstores, a tin shop and Washington Hotel. Along the west side stand Robins Motor Co. garage, Riverview Hotel, the temporary public school, the Baptist Church with its Sunday school, Central Laundry and the fire department's building. Soden's Garage stands at the top right. East of Farnsworth Avenue the lots run to Miles Alley and Hankins Alley, with a junk yard, a garage and machine shop (concrete block), and cement products works toward the bottom. Crosswicks Street leaves Farnsworth Avenue diagonally at the bottom, lined with the City Hall, fire house and dwellings. The compass is at the lower left.
notes: Printed West Park and East Park are the two sides of Park Street / West Park Street in OpenStreetMap.
Miles Alley is Miles Avenue in OpenStreetMap; its junction with Farnsworth Avenue was rejected by the fit (8 m) and not used.

Railroad Avenue and Crosswicks Street were left out of the control: Railroad Avenue is drawn offset on both sides of the railroad, and the Farnsworth Avenue / Walnut Street / Crosswicks Street node has two OpenStreetMap nodes 20 m apart.

Downtown Farnsworth Avenue between Park and Walnut Streets, Prince Street to 2nd Street; north up-right; 50 ft. Configured by a helper. Railroad Avenue (rails in the street) and Crosswicks Street left out.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, and covers the north-eastern side of Bordentown between 2nd Street at the left and Spring Street at the right. Mary Street, Ann Street and Elizabeth Street run across the lower part; East Park and Railroad Avenue cross the top and middle. The upper half is taken up by the Bordentown Military Institute: its student dormitories on both sides of 3rd Street, class rooms, dormitories with dining room and kitchen, bowling alleys, drill hall, hospital, laundry and a tailor shop, with a north-west block of the campus drawn as block 128. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Trenton Division) runs diagonally across the sheet in a cut below the institute, with a gate tower beside Railroad Avenue. South of it stand W. A. Shreve & Co. coal yard, J. M. Reeder & Co. coal yard on a siding, the Bordentown Milling Co. grist mill, Joseph Popkin's junk yard and the Chase Apartments. Between Ann Street and Mary Street are a lumber shed, a feed warehouse and rows of brick-filled dwellings, and the blocks between Mary Street and Elizabeth Street are almost entirely dwellings. Vacant land fills the top and the right edge. The compass is at the right and the scale bar at the lower left.
notes: The lettering at the top reads Third Street and elsewhere 3rd Street, both for the same street.
Railroad Avenue was left out of the control because OpenStreetMap shows a railroad in it and the junctions came out 3 to 4 m off.

Bordentown Military Institute, Ann, Mary, Elizabeth Streets between 2nd/3rd and Spring Streets, Bordentown Milling Co.; north up-right; 50 ft. Configured by a helper. Railroad Avenue left out (rails in the street).

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 is the main part of sheet 7, below the heavy diagonal line that cuts off two industrial insets, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. It covers the north-eastern edge of Bordentown from Pine Street south to Spring Street, between Ann Street and Mary Street on the west and Elizabeth Street on the east. Mary Street and Elizabeth Street are lined with one- and two-storey frame and brick-filled dwellings, with barns and sheds behind. The large open block between the Pennsylvania Railroad and Mary Street is the athletic field of the Bordentown Military Institute. At the lower left, at Ann Street and Spring Street, stands the factory building of the Union Overall Mfg. Co. East of Elizabeth Street are the kilns of a specialty porcelain works. A creek runs across the upper left corner below the dividing line, and the railroad tracks run down the left side of the part, with a picket fence along them. Lafayette Street crosses the middle of the part, and water pipes of 4 and 8 inches are drawn in Mary Street and Spring Street.
notes: The two insets above the heavy line (The Independent Brick Co. Plants No. 2 and No. 3) are parts 2 and 3 and were not placed: neither has a street junction.

Three parts, 50 ft. Part 1 (main, below the heavy diagonal line): Pine Street to Spring Street, Ann Street to Elizabeth Street, Bordentown Military Institute athletic field, Union Overall Mfg Co. Part 2 (inset, top left): The Independent Brick Co. Plant No. 3, located 1/4 mile NE of City Hall, on Public Road: no junction, not placed. Part 3 (inset, top right): The Independent Brick Co. Plant No. 2, Fieldsboro, 2 miles SW of City Hall, on Burlington Road: no junction, not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Independent Brick Co. Plant No. 3, 1/4 mile NE of City Hall, on Public Road (no street junction; needs identification of Public Road and the siding).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Independent Brick Co. Plant No. 2, Fieldsboro, on Burlington Road (no street junction; needs a junction or parcel corners on Burlington Road).

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 is the right half of sheet 8, east of a heavy line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the south-western edge of Bordentown along West Burlington Street between Pine Street, marked not opened, and Willow Street, with Oliver Street parallel to it and Federal Street and Anderson Avenue crossing. Federal Street is drawn twice: a diagonal stretch at the top running toward Black Creek, which is lettered in the upper left corner, and a short horizontal stretch between Oliver Street and Willow Street. The blocks hold rows of two- and three-storey frame and brick-filled dwellings, many lots still open toward Pine Street, with barns, sheds and a green house behind. Lot numbers in the 300s are printed along Oliver Street and Willow Street. The part adjoins sheet 9 to the east, sheet 4 to the north and sheet 13 beyond Black Creek.
notes: Federal Street is drawn in two stretches; it was not used for control.
Fitted scale is 7.67 px/ft from four junctions in a rectangle, 3 percent below the atlas value.
Pine is marked not opened; West Pine Street in OpenStreetMap meets West Burlington Street here.
The left half of the sheet (part 2: W. Swift Jr. Inc. machine shop and Springfield Worsted Mills on East Park, Ward, Green and Swifts Lane) has no surviving junction and was not placed.

Two parts, 50 ft, north up-right, divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (right): West Burlington Street between Pine (not opened) and Willow Streets, Oliver Street, Federal Street, Anderson Avenue; four junctions only, scale 3 percent low. Part 2 (left): W. Swift Jr. Inc. machine shop and Springfield Worsted Mills on East Park, Ward, Green and Swifts Lane, by the Harris H. Hammond grounds: no surviving junction, not placed. Configured by a helper as one part; split by the lead.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: left half: W. Swift Jr. Inc. machine shop and Springfield Worsted Mills on East Park, Ward, Green and Swifts Lane (no surviving street junction (Ward and Green not in OpenStreetMap here); needs parcel corners along Park Street or features carried from sheet 3 or 6).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the business centre of Bordentown on both sides of Farnsworth Avenue and Prince Street, between Walnut Street on the west and Burlington Street on the east, with the wedge between Crosswicks Street and West Street reaching north to Borden Street and 2nd Street, and Willow Street along the bottom. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. The blocks along Farnsworth Avenue are lined with brick and frame stores and dwellings, many of two and three storeys, numbered 300 to 369. Named buildings include the First National Bank and Trinity M.E. Church on the north side of Farnsworth Avenue, the Roleir Shirt Co. factory on the south side, a garage, an ice cream pavilion and a bake house. Between Crosswicks Street and West Street lies the J. G. Chamberlain lumber yard with its lumber sheds, wagon shed and storage buildings, and a long building marked autos. In the south-east corner, on Willow Street, is the E. B. Tantum lumber yard. Prince Street is lined with rows of two and two-and-a-half storey brick-filled dwellings. Federal Street is drawn as a narrow street about 20 feet wide that crosses Farnsworth Avenue and turns diagonally south of Prince Street. Water pipes are drawn in the streets with their sizes, and the sheet carries a scale of feet below Prince Street.
notes: Federal Street is drawn about 20 ft wide; it was left out of the control points.
East Burlington and West Burlington are East Burlington Street and West Burlington Street in OpenStreetMap; Crosswicks is Crosswicks Street, West is West Street, Borden is Borden Street.

Pilot. Farnsworth Avenue and Prince Street between Walnut Street and Burlington Street, Crosswicks Street, Borden Street; 50 ft; north up-left (rotation about -59). Federal Street is drawn 20 ft wide and left out.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers the east side of Bordentown, where Crosswicks Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Elizabeth Street runs down the left edge, with Lafayette Street and Spring Street across the top. Borden Street and Hopkinson Street branch to the south-east from Crosswicks Street, and West Street crosses them; East Burlington Street runs down the right edge with Leyden Avenue and Myrtle Avenue off it. Large public buildings stand along Crosswicks Street: the Bordentown High School with gymnasium and auditorium, the Public School with a kindergarten, St. Mary's R. C. Church with chapel, St. Mary's Hall and School, a city fire station, Mt. Zion A. M. E. Church and a school at the top right. Thomas & Bowker granite and monument works lies below the high school. The blocks along Elizabeth Street, Borden Street and West Street are small dwellings; the blocks near the top between Lafayette Street and Spring Street are mostly open. The compass is at the left centre and the scale bar at the bottom. The block at the lower left meets sheet 5 at 2nd Street.
notes: The junction of Elizabeth Street and Lafayette Street was detected 15 m from the fit and rejected; the part rests on eleven other junctions.
Hopkinson Street and Borden Street reach Crosswicks Street at junctions read from the street edges on the sheet.
Crosswicks Street diagonal, Lafayette, Spring, Elizabeth, Hopkinson, Borden, West and East Burlington Streets; north up-left; 50 ft. Configured by a helper.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, and covers the south-eastern edge of the town, the blocks east and west of Farnsworth Avenue, which runs across the middle of the sheet. From left to right the cross streets are East and West Burlington Street, East and West Union Street and East and West Chestnut Street; Carpenter Street and Reeder Avenue cross the top and Prince Street and Willow Street the lower half. The upper left holds the Bordentown Dairy Co., the Jacob Holzbaur Vienna steam bakery and an artificial ice manufacturing plant, with dwellings along East Burlington Street. Farnsworth Avenue carries the Presbyterian Church, the Humane Fire Co. and Hope Hose Co. building and dwellings. East of Union Street the blocks are mostly dwellings with deep lots, a hollow tile plant, Coopers Alley and a green house at the bottom. Block numbers 24 to 26, 50 to 55 and 100 are shown; Prince Street is marked 60 ft wide and Willow Street 50 ft wide. The compass is at the lower left. Part of Anderson Avenue and block 133 appear at the bottom, with a connection to sheet 8.
notes: East Burlington Street and West Burlington Street were left out of the control: their drawn line bends along the left edge and the junctions came out 2 to 5 m off.
The fitted scale is 7.65 pixels per foot, 3.5 percent below the atlas value; Union Street to Chestnut Street is drawn about 8 percent shorter than today's streets, so the east side may be displaced.

Farnsworth Avenue with East Burlington, Union and Chestnut Streets, Carpenter, Prince, Willow, Reeder Avenue; Bordentown Dairy Co., artificial ice works, Presbyterian Church; north up-left; 50 ft. Chestnut Street is drawn only to its west edge at the sheet edge: its four junctions were hand-picked (edge plus 30 ft). Burlington Streets left out (bending edge).

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 is the upper half of sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, at the eastern edge of Bordentown. It covers East Burlington Street at the top, Leyden Avenue and Myrtle Avenue running south to East Union Street, and the fork where Crosswicks Street and Butts Avenue leave town to the south-east, with the end of East Chestnut Street at the left. North points to the upper right. The built-up blocks along East Burlington Street, Leyden Avenue, Myrtle Avenue and East Union Street hold mostly one- and two-storey frame dwellings, with small lots along the streets. Between Crosswicks Street and Lafayette Street stands the Monastery of St. Clare, a brick building with a chapel. South of East Union Street the land is open: large undivided blocks with a few scattered dwellings, a greenhouse and outbuildings. A dash-dot line marks the city line, and a 6 inch water pipe runs south across the open ground. The lower edge of the part is the heavy line dividing it from the second part of the sheet.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch; north up-right, turned 90 degrees from sheet 9.
The junction of East Union Street and Leyden Avenue was detected on another line and rejected; the part rests on six other junctions.

Two parts, 100 ft to an inch, divided by a heavy horizontal line. Part 1 (upper): East Burlington Street, Leyden and Myrtle Avenues, East Union Street, Crosswicks Street, Butts Avenue, Monastery of St. Clare; north up-right. Part 2 (lower): Farnsworth Avenue from Chestnut Street to Cemetery Road (today Municipal Drive), Mill Street, a brook; north up-left; three points along Farnsworth Avenue (helmert).

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 is the lower half of sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and shows Farnsworth Avenue running south-east out of Bordentown from Chestnut Street to Cemetery Road. North points to the upper left, as on the town sheets. The land on both sides is thinly built: a few frame dwellings, barns and sheds along Farnsworth Avenue and Mill Street, large open blocks and a group of dwellings and outbuildings near the right edge. A brook crosses Farnsworth Avenue near the left edge and runs south. A dash-dot line marks the city line along Mill Street. Lot numbers in the 700s are printed along Farnsworth Avenue. The bottom and right edges are marked no exposure.
notes: Cemetery Road meets Farnsworth Avenue where Municipal Drive does today (416 m from Chestnut Street on both); Municipal Drive was used as its modern name.
Placed from three junctions along Farnsworth Avenue only (helmert); low confidence across the street.

Two parts, 100 ft to an inch, divided by a heavy horizontal line. Part 1 (upper): East Burlington Street, Leyden and Myrtle Avenues, East Union Street, Crosswicks Street, Butts Avenue, Monastery of St. Clare; north up-right. Part 2 (lower): Farnsworth Avenue from Chestnut Street to Cemetery Road (today Municipal Drive), Mill Street, a brook; north up-left; three points along Farnsworth Avenue (helmert).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left and shows the grounds of the State Manual Training & Industrial School for Colored Youth, south of Black's Creek between the Delaware River and Burlington Pike. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs along the river at the left in a bundle of tracks, and Burlington Pike, 66 feet wide, runs down the right side of the sheet from the creek. The school's buildings stand in open grounds crossed by footpaths and private roads: the Administration Building, boys' dormitories including Gregory Hall, a girls' dormitory, a block with dining room, gymnasium and auditorium, the Trades Building with carpentry, machine, painting and printing shops, a recreation house, a laundry, a green house and scattered dwellings, with water pipes laid between them; a 100,000 gallon water tank stands on an iron tower, and near the creek are a pump house and a pump vault marked not used. Front Street enters at the lower left, where the sheet meets sheet 14. Much of the sheet is open field and the bottom edge is marked vacant beyond. The sheet carries its own scale bar of 100 feet to one inch.
notes: No street junction on the sheet. Placed from two points on Burlington Pike (today West Burlington Street and Burlington Road): its crossing of Black's Creek carried from sheet 3 part 2, and a point 659 m down the modern road at the printed scale. The drawn railroad lies 1 to 7 m from the modern River Line through this placement. Low confidence.

State Manual Training & Industrial School for Colored Youth grounds between the Delaware River (Pennsylvania Railroad) and Burlington Pike (today West Burlington Street / Burlington Road), south of Black's Creek; 100 ft; north up-left. No junction: placed from Burlington Pike (creek crossing carried from sheet 3 part 2, plus a point down the modern road); the drawn railroad agrees with the River Line to 1 to 7 m.

sheet-14-1.description: Part 1 is the lower part of sheet 14, below a heavy line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It shows the strip between the Delaware River and Front Street south-west of the State Manual Training School, crossed by the many tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad, Trenton Division. South of the tracks stand the works of the Ironside Pottery Co. (sanitary ware), with its kilns and shipping building, the White Hill Chain Works, marked closed, and the large manufacturing and pickling buildings of the Bordentown Steel & Tube Corp'n, with its storage building, hydrants and a 20,000 gallon wood water tank. Along Front Street lie State property and a few rows of two- and two-and-a-half-storey dwellings. The part adjoins sheet 13 at the right; the two brick works above the heavy line are separate insets.
notes: No street junction. Anchored on the Bordentown Steel & Tube water tank, carried from sheet 13, with the atlas scale and a north direction of 39.7 degrees taken from the bearing of the modern River Line; the drawn tracks lie 1 to 7 m from it. Low confidence.

Parts 2 and 3 (insets above the heavy line): Church Brick Co. Plant No. 2 (left) and Plant No. 1 (right) on the Delaware River: no street, not placed.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows the south-western end of Fieldsboro along the Delaware River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Washington Street crosses the sheet from left to right, with Front Street and 2nd Street running down the sheet and Delaware Avenue along the bottom, set diagonally. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Trenton Division) runs down the left side beside a dock and the Delaware River, with a passenger station and freight station. Between the railroad and Front Street stand two large works: Bordentown Forge & Machine Co., closed, with a forge shop, Chas. Warner Co. machine shop and the lessee's machine shop, and the American Ammonia Co. with its engine and compressor house, ammonia tanks and storage of empty cylinders. A steep bank separates these plants from the street grid. East of Front Street the blocks 136 to 142 are almost empty, the Fieldsboro Public School stands in block 142 and a few dwellings and a grand stand lie along 2nd Street. Rhea's Alley runs east to west across the top. Arbitrary Place runs beside block 141. The compass is at the right and the scale bar at the lower right.
notes: Only three junctions were found (Front / Washington, 2nd / Washington and 2nd / Delaware), so the part is an exact fit with no check; low confidence.
Washington Street, Front Street and 2nd Street are drawn as one street on both sides of their junctions, which OpenStreetMap names North and South Front Street and North and South 2nd Street.

Delaware Avenue / South 2nd Street is drawn about 156 m from Washington Street along 2nd Street, against 119 m today: the modern junction was left out, and the sheet is placed from two junctions on Washington Street only (helmert, low confidence).

Fieldsboro: Washington, Front and 2nd Streets, Delaware (drawn 37 m from the modern Delaware Avenue junction, left out), Bordentown Forge & Machine Co., American Ammonia Co., Pennsylvania Railroad along the Delaware River; north up-left; 50 ft; placed from two junctions on Washington Street (helmert).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows the main built area of Fieldsboro, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Washington Street runs down the sheet from the top, crossed by 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets, with Delaware Avenue on the left, running down the sheet and meeting 4th and 5th Streets. The blocks between Washington Street and Delaware Avenue are narrow lots with small dwellings, and the Fieldsboro Post Office stands on Washington Street. On 5th Street are the Baptist Church and its belfry, with a dwelling and church grounds beside it. Lockwood Avenue runs south-east from 5th Street past a green house and sheds to vacant land at the bottom. The M. E. Church and a horse shed stand near 2nd Street at the upper left. East of Washington Street lie blocks 143, 144, 148 to 151 and 154 to 156, with Lines Alley and Rhea's Alley crossing them and a windmill on a steel tower in block 155. The streets change angle across the sheet. A compass at the lower right shows north up-right; a heavy outline surrounds the edge toward sheet 15.
notes: 4th Street here is Burlington Street in OpenStreetMap.
The junction of Burlington Street with Delaware Avenue (East Delaware Road) was detected 9.6 m from the fit of the other points and was excluded; low confidence on the left side of the sheet.
Leave-one-out error is 9 m because four of five junctions lie along Washington Street.

Fieldsboro: Washington Street with 2nd to 5th Streets (4th is today Burlington Street) and Delaware Avenue, M.E. Church, post office; north up-right; 50 ft. Configured by a helper; four of five points along Washington Street.
